subject: Hosted eval: sandbox -> prod SLAs & endpoint mapping
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood-inference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina@scriptly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted eval: sandbox -> prod SLAs & endpoint mapping

Thanks for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Per our call I wanted to capture the recommended path for a hosted evaluation and clarify the quickstart items so your ops and infra teams can plan. Actionable items at the top, details below.

Attachments: SOW_v1.pdf (draft), rate_estimate.xlsx (ballpark)

Top actions
- We will provision sandbox credentials and a staging endpoint (one week sandbox window) — Redwood action: provide creds within 48 hours.
- Scriptly to validate two representative payloads (chat and document summarization) and send sample traces — Scriptly action: attach to this thread.
- Confirm expected steady-state: if you expect >500 reqs/s sustained we recommend evaluating Dedicated; otherwise Hosted is optimal to iterate quickly.

Quickstart / endpoint mapping (hosted)
- Sandbox endpoints:
  - /v1/chat (streaming) — for conversational flows, recommended for session-based UX
  - /v1/generate (non-streaming) — for batch summarization and reranks
  - /v1/embeddings — for vectoring search features
- Rate guidance for initial eval (sandbox):
  - Soft limit: 200 requests/min per API key (sufficient for initial functional testing)
  - Burst window: up to 2k requests over 5 minutes for smoke tests; sustained bursts will be throttled to protect other tenants
  - Token throughput guidance: aim for <50k tokens/min in sandbox until we verify sequence-length distributions
- Production pilot suggestions:
  - Start with a 2-week pilot on Hosted with a controlled traffic slice (we can map 10% traffic through Redwood for a canary)
  - For predictable SLA and consistent latency at scale, Dedicated capacity is recommended once you exceed a sustained 5–10M tokens/day or need guaranteed GPU isolation

Caching and statefulness
- Prefix/KV caching: we can enable request-level prefix cache for repeated prompts (helps reduce token cost for deterministic responses). This is transparent in Hosted and configurable per-route.
- Session stickiness: for low-latency conversational UX you can enable session affinity; we'll provide a small sample proxy config for your infra team.

Security / residency note
- Hosted keeps logs for debugging for up to 30 days by default; we can disable request logging for PII flows and provide field-level masking guidance. If you need VPC/private deployment for data residency we can propose Redwood Private with our packaged on-prem option.

Next steps (timeline)
- Redwood: sandbox creds + sample endpoint mapping doc (48 hours)
- Scriptly: share payloads and compliance questions (2 business days)
- Joint: quick sync after sandbox smoke test (end of next week)

Cheers,
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Nina Patel <nina@scriptly.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Scriptly Ops <ops@scriptly.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted eval: sandbox -> prod SLAs & endpoint mapping

Thanks Priyom — super helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) KV/prefix cache behavior — can you confirm whether cached responses count against token billing? We have some high-volume deterministic prompts and need to understand cost behavior.

2) Session stickiness — our product uses short-lived sessions (~3–5 minutes) and rehydrates context from our store between requests. Is the session affinity you mentioned required, or would we be safe rehydrating each call (trade-off: latency vs infra complexity)?

3) Compliance: we need confirmation that request bodies flagged as PII can be excluded from logging and that you support contractual language for data not to be used for model training. Our legal lead (cc'ed on internal) will request a redline of the SOW.

We will attach two sample payloads (1x chat, 1x summarization) to this thread by EOD. Also curious on typical latency numbers for streaming chat endpoints at ~50 concurrent sessions.

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Product
Scriptly Inc

Nice summary — a few operational answers to Nina's questions below.

Nina — quick answers:
- Cached responses and billing: prefix/KV cache prevents model execution when we can serve a deterministically cached response; cached responses are not billed for tokens. However, cache hit logic depends on route-level configuration (you can set TTLs and key derivation). We'll include a short guide for your infra team showing how cacheable keys map to request hashes.
- Session strategy: if you rehydrate context each call, you'll pay full token cost but avoid affinity complexity. If you want lower token cost and lower latency for active sessions, enable session affinity + local KV cache — this saves tokens for repeated context but requires sticky routing for concurrency. For 3–5 minute sessions, affinity is usually worth it if you have many repeated turns per session.
- PII and training: Hosted offers a contractual option to opt-out of data usage for training and we provide field-level masking on request logs. We'll mark the SOW accordingly and legal can include a data handling addendum.

Latency expectations (hosted streaming chat, ~50 concurrent sessions)
- Median latency (first-byte streaming): 120–220ms for Llama2-class models on our multi-tenant hosted pool, depending on sequence length.
- Tail (.95): 400–700ms for long context windows; Dedicated reduces tail latency variance by ~30% in our measurements.

Pilot recommendations
- We'll spin up the sandbox endpoints within 48 hours as Priyom mentioned. After you validate payloads we can enable a 2-week pilot routing 10% of production traffic to Hosted. If the pilot shows stable throughput and you prefer lower unit cost, we will provide a Dedicated sizing proposal (based on measured tokens/day and concurrency).

I'll queue the SOW redline and flag the data-training opt-out clause. Priyom / Soojin will follow up with the sandbox creds and a short ops playbook.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
